title: 2023年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound(充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem. Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities(便利设施). Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.

P2 This is reflected in our homes. The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size. By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. What's more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.

P3 There are consequences of living big. As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. Take swimming pools. While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.

P4 The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?

P5 I believe neither is acceptable. We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces. A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.

questions.q: What are big houses promoted to be in the United States?
options: A luxury for the homeless.
A reward for industriousness.
An abundant source of comforts.
An absolute necessity for happiness.
questions.explain:
【判型】Q46 问的是 What are big houses promoted to be，要的是文中明写的一个事实陈述，不 需推理。

【拆句】Q46 是一个被动语态疑问句，主干为"big houses are promoted to be 什么"，promoted to be 后面接的内容就是答案要补的成分，结构平铺，无陷阱。 46. What are big houses promoted to be in the United States? A) A luxury for the homeless. B) A reward for industriousness. C) An abundant source of comforts. D) An absolute necessity for happiness.

【定位】Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury. 大房子被宣传成对努力工作和勤勉的一种回报，把住房从基本必需品变成了奢侈品。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文宣传是面向勤奋者的回报，A luxury for the homeless 把奢侈品安到 homeless 头 上，而原文 homelessness 只是危机背景，并非大房子的宣传对象。 B) ✓ 正确 a reward for hard work and diligence ↔A reward for industriousness 预判的"对勤奋的回报"在 A reward for industriousness 中 reward 与 industriousness 双双对应，锁定该项。 C) 答非所问 An abundant source of comforts 取自第三段及背景里 amenities/abound 的语义， 但 Q46 问的是大房子被"宣传成什么"，定位句给的是 reward，不是"舒适之源"。 D) 与原文相反 原文恰恰说大房子使住房 from a basic necessity into a luxury（从必需变奢侈），An absolute necessity for happiness 反把它说成"幸福的绝对必需品"，与原文相反。 住大房子的后果之一是什么？ A) 许多美国人的生活质量变得更低了。 B) 来自不同背景的人们不再社交了。 C) 人们不再能使用公共游泳池了。 D) 许多美国人的私人生活受到了负面影响。

questions.q: What is one of the consequences of living big?
options: Many Americans' quality of life has become lower.
People from diverse backgrounds no longer socialize.
People no longer have access to public swimming pools.
Many Americans' private life has been negatively affected.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one of the consequences 用 one of 限定，答案是原文列举的多项后果中的一 项，属可直接定位的细节。

【拆句】Q47 主干为"What is one of the consequences"，of living big 是后置定语修饰 consequences，one of 提示原文有多项后果，结构简单。

【定位】Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. 第二，曾经的公共空间——不同背景的人过去常在此相聚——日益被私有化，导致面向所有 人的公共设施数量减少，许多人的生活质量随之下降。 47. What is one of the consequences of living big? A) Many Americans' quality of life has become lower. B) People from diverse backgrounds no longer socialize. C) People no longer have access to public swimming pools. D) Many Americans' private life has been negatively affected.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 a reduced quality of life for many ↔Many Americans' quality of life has become lower 预判的"生活质量下降"与 quality of life has become lower 字面同义，直接锁定。 B) 过度推断 原文只说公共空间被私有化、不同背景的人"过去"常相聚（used to），并未说人们 no longer socialize（彻底不再社交），属过度引申。 C) 以偏概全 游泳池只是说明私有化的一个例子，原文说 public municipal pools were often closed（常被关闭），no longer have access to public swimming pools 把"常被 关"绝对成"再也用不上"，且以个例顶替本题要的总后果。 D) 偷换概念 原文受影响的是 quality of life（生活质量），private life has been negatively affected 偷换成 private life（私人生活），概念不同。 住大房子引发了什么问题？ A) 与道德原则相关的问题。 B) 与劳动力成本有关的问题。 C) 关于提倡什么样的生活方式的问题。 D) 关于住房发展的问题。

questions.q: What questions arise from living big?
options: Questions related to moral principles.
Questions having to do with labor cost.
Questions about what lifestyle to promote.
Questions concerning housing development.
questions.explain:
【判型】What questions arise from living big 问的是原文明确点出的问题性质，文中有直接对应 的形容词限定，属细节。

【拆句】Q48 主干"What questions arise"，from living big 为原因状语，整句问"住大房子引发哪 类问题"，无复杂从句。

【定位】The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. 因此，住房越来越大的趋势引出了伦理（道德）层面的问题。 48. What questions arise from living big? A) Questions related to moral principles. B) Questions having to do with labor cost. C) Questions about what lifestyle to promote. D) Questions concerning housing development.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 ethical questions ↔Questions related to moral principles 预判的"伦理/道德问题"与 moral principles 同义，直接锁定。 B) 答非所问 labor cost 取自第四段反问里 using the low-wage labor of others，但那只是伦理问 题的内容举例，问题的"性质"是伦理性，labor cost 答非所问。 C) 张冠李戴 lifestyle to promote 接近第五段"该提倡什么生活方式"的话题，但 Q48 问的是第四段 引发的问题性质，what lifestyle to promote 张冠李戴到了下一段内容。 D) 无中生有 housing development（住房开发/发展）在第四段问题里并无对应表述，原文谈的是 伦理而非开发问题，属凭空捏造。 作者认为什么样的社会制度是不可接受的？ A) 一个富人剥削建造他们房屋的低工资劳动者的制度。 B) 一个富人以越来越难以证明合理的价格购买便利设施的制度。 C) 一个上层阶级剥夺下层阶级负担得起的住房的制度。 D) 一个富人以穷人为代价享受更舒适生活的制度。

questions.q: What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable?
options: One in which the wealthy exploit the low-wage laborers building their houses.
One in which the rich purchase amenities at an increasingly unjustifiable price.
One in which the upper classes deprive the lower classes of affordable housing.
One in which the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor.
questions.explain:
【判型】What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable 答案在原文有 a system in which... 的直接描述，是可定位的细节，而非需推断的整体态度。

【拆句】Q49 主干"What kind of social system is unacceptable"，中间插入 does the author think 表明这是作者的判断，从句嵌套但语义清晰：找作者认为不可接受的那种制度。

【定位】Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor? 我们是否愿意接受这样一种制度：富人购买的便利设施增加，就意味着穷人可享的便利设施 减少？ 49. What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable? A) One in which the wealthy exploit the low-wage laborers building their houses. B) One in which the rich purchase amenities at an increasingly unjustifiable price. C) One in which the upper classes deprive the lower classes of affordable housing. D) One in which the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文第一个反问确提到 using the low-wage labor of others，但 the low-wage laborers building their houses 把"他人的低薪劳动"窄化为"盖房工人"，且第二个反问 （富人便利↔穷人便利）才是更完整的对应，A 项以偏概全。 B) 无中生有 原文说富人购买便利使穷人便利减少，从未谈 an increasingly unjustifiable price（越 来越不合理的价格），价格维度是捏造的。 C) 偷换概念 deprive the lower classes of affordable housing（剥夺下层的平价住房）取自首段背 景 Affordable housing is inadequate，但作者第四段否定的制度是"便利的增减对 立"，不是剥夺平价住房，概念被偷换。 D) ✓ 正确 an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor ↔the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor 预判的"富人享乐、穷人受损"恰是 enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor 的含义，锁定该项。 作者提倡人们怎样才能生活得好？ A) 找到将私人空间转变为公共空间的方法。 B) 建造更多那些不太富裕的人负担得起的房屋。 C) 创造更多供每个人享受的公共空间。 D) 让所有便利设施对富人和穷人一样可及。

questions.q: What does the author advocate for people to live well?
options: Finding ways to turn private spaces into public ones.
Building more houses affordable to those less affluent.
More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy.
All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author advocate 答案是末段作者直接给出的建议，有明写对应句，属细 节定位题。

【拆句】Q50 主干"What does the author advocate"，for people to live well 是目的状语（为了 让人们住得好），整句问"作者为此提倡什么"，结构清楚。

【定位】A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all. 比起为少数人盖更大的房子，更好的目标是为所有人创造更多可公共使用的空间与设施。 50. What does the author advocate for people to live well? A) Finding ways to turn private spaces into public ones. B) Building more houses affordable to those less affluent. C) More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy. D) All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike.

【选项】A) 无中生有 作者主张是"创造更多公共空间"，并未说要把私人空间 turn private spaces into public ones（改造成公共空间），这一具体做法原文没有。 B) 与原文相反 Building more houses affordable 回到了"盖房子"，而作者主张的恰恰是别再盖大 房子、转向公共空间，且 affordable housing 是首段背景非作者的提倡，方向与主张 相悖。 C) ✓ 正确 create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all ↔ More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy 预判的"为人人创造公共空间"与 More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy 字面同义，锁定该项。 D) 偷换概念 原文是"为所有人创造公共空间与设施"，All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike 用 All amenities 把范围绝对化为"所有便利设施都对贫富开放"，超 出作者所说的"公共空间"范围。
